validation_history.validation_error: Evidence URL for sample_size must use pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov

validated_results.title: Alcohol intake increases high-grade prostate cancer risk among men taking dutasteride in the REDUCE trial.
validated_results.reason: This prospective cohort analysis within the REDUCE trial evaluated the association between alcohol consumption and prostate cancer risk with complete risk estimates and multivariable adjustment.

extraction.population: Men aged 50-75 with PSA 2.5-10.0 ng/ml and a prior negative prostate biopsy enrolled in the REDUCE trial

sample_size.excerpt: Analysis included 6374 REDUCE participants, including 998 and 435 men diagnosed with low-grade or high-grade PCa, respectively.

p_value.excerpt: In contrast, men randomized to dutasteride and reporting more than seven drinks per week were 86% more likely to be diagnosed with high-grade PCa ( p = 0.01).

comparison.excerpt: Alcohol intake was analyzed as a continuous variable (units per week) and also categorized to represent nondrinkers (0 U/wk), moderate drinkers ( 7 U/wk) and heavy drinkers (>7 U/wk).

design.excerpt: Reduction by Dutasteride of Prostate Cancer Events was a 4-yr, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to compare PCa after dutasteride administration (0.5 mg/d) with placebo.

timing.excerpt: Participants had a baseline prostate-specific antigen between 2.5 and 10.0 ng/ml and a recent negative prostate biopsy. Alcohol intake was determined by baseline questionnaire, and participants underwent a prostate biopsy to determine PCa status at 2 yr and 4 yr of follow-up.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: All REDUCE participants in this analysis completed a medical history questionnaire prior to randomization, including age, race, smoking, medication use, and alcohol use. Intake of beer, wine, and liquor was converted to standard units of alcoholic drinks per week
